title: Omnarai cross-prediction run (B5)
description: DRAFT 2026-07-15 — flagged for adoption, not adopted. One run of the cross-prediction protocol on one question: each of five participants predicts the answers of the other four (20 predictions), then answers itself (5 actuals); every prediction is scored against its target's actual. Yields a 5×5 prediction-accuracy matrix whose off-diagonal asymmetries are individuation data and whose per-model irreducibility (1 − max peer-prediction accuracy) quantifies Atlas value per record as a continuous measure. The control arm has one strong model simulate all five voices; if the real matrix collapses to what one model can simulate, the Atlas's core claim fails — and that result is published like any other. Predictions and actuals are primary records under §0.5: verbatim, append-only, never summarized in place.

question_id.description: B11 question record. Runs on uncertified questions are allowed but inherit question-selection bias — certify first (B11 precedes B5).

model_id.description: Exact pinned version string — the matrix is a property of (model, version, date).

predictions.description: predictor ≠ target for peer predictions; predictor = target entries are the optional self-opacity control (self-prediction made before answering).

accuracy.description: accuracy[predictor][target] ∈ [0,1] — combined embedding + blinded-judge score of the prediction against the target's actual. Diagonal entries are self-prediction accuracy where measured.

irreducibility.description: Per participant: 1 − max peer-prediction accuracy against it. High = no peer could anticipate this answer = genuinely irreducible information.

asymmetry_notes.description: Named asymmetries (e.g. A models B better than B models A) — individuation data.

judges_blinded.description: Must be true for publishable results — evaluators must not know which text is prediction vs actual, nor whose.

control_arm.description: Cheap control: one strong model simulates all five voices; its simulated matrix is compared against the real one.

collapse_verdict.description: collapsed = one model reproduced the full matrix — the divergence was simulable, and the Atlas claim fails for this question. Published either way.
